---
title: "All-Time MLB Home Run Leaders"
format: html
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false
---

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(Lahman)
library(plotly)
library(DT)
library(crosstalk)

team_franchises <- Teams |>
  select(yearID, teamID, franchID, name) |>
  distinct(yearID, teamID, .keep_all = TRUE)

franchise_labels <- Teams |>
  arrange(yearID) |>
  group_by(franchID) |>
  summarise(franchise = last(name), .groups = "drop")

player_seasons <- Batting |>
  left_join(team_franchises, by = c("yearID", "teamID")) |>
  group_by(playerID, yearID) |>
  summarise(
    season_hr = sum(HR, na.rm = TRUE),
    season_g = sum(G, na.rm = TRUE),
    season_ab = sum(AB, na.rm = TRUE),
    season_rbi = sum(RBI, na.rm = TRUE),
    primary_franch = franchID[which.max(G)],
    .groups = "drop"
  )

top_leaders <- player_seasons |>
  group_by(playerID) |>
  summarise(
    career_hr = sum(season_hr),
    games = sum(season_g),
    at_bats = sum(season_ab),
    career_rbi = sum(season_rbi),
    peak_season_hr = max(season_hr),
    peak_year = yearID[which.max(season_hr)],
    first_year = min(yearID),
    last_year = max(yearID),
    franchID = names(sort(table(primary_franch), decreasing = TRUE))[1],
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  slice_max(career_hr, n = 30, with_ties = TRUE) |>
  left_join(People |> select(playerID, nameFirst, nameLast, bats), by = "playerID") |>
  left_join(franchise_labels, by = "franchID") |>
  arrange(desc(career_hr), games) |>
  mutate(
    rank = min_rank(desc(career_hr)),
    player_name = if_else(playerID == "griffke02", "Ken Griffey Jr.", paste(nameFirst, nameLast)),
    years_active = paste0(first_year, "–", last_year),
    peak_label = paste0(peak_season_hr, " (", peak_year, ")"),
    hr_per_162 = round(162 * career_hr / games, 1),
    ab_per_hr = round(at_bats / career_hr, 1),
    bats_label = case_when(
      bats == "L" ~ "Left",
      bats == "R" ~ "Right",
      bats == "B" ~ "Switch",
      TRUE ~ "Right"
    ),
    era = factor(
      case_when(
        last_year < 1960 ~ "Pre-Expansion (before 1960)",
        last_year < 1995 ~ "Expansion Era (1960–1994)",
        TRUE ~ "Modern Era (1995–present)"
      ),
      levels = c(
        "Pre-Expansion (before 1960)",
        "Expansion Era (1960–1994)",
        "Modern Era (1995–present)"
      )
    )
  ) |>
  mutate(player = factor(player_name, levels = rev(player_name))) |>
  select(
    rank, player, franchise, era, bats_label, years_active,
    career_hr, peak_season_hr, peak_label, hr_per_162, ab_per_hr, career_rbi, games
  )

shared_leaders <- SharedData$new(top_leaders, key = ~player, group = "hr_leaders")

era_colors <- c(
  "Pre-Expansion (before 1960)" = "#1b9e77",
  "Expansion Era (1960–1994)" = "#d95f02",
  "Modern Era (1995–present)" = "#2c7fb8"
)
```

## MLB's All-Time Home Run Kings

Reaching the summit of Major League Baseball's career home run leaderboard demands an extraordinary blend of **single-season peak power** and **two-decade durability**. Only **28 hitters in MLB history** have joined the exclusive **500 Home Run Club**, and just four—**Barry Bonds (762)**, **Hank Aaron (755)**, **Babe Ruth (714)**, and **Albert Pujols (703)**—have ever eclipsed 700 career homers. Notably, ballpark environment plays a fascinating role even at the top: Barry Bonds hit the majority of his late-career homers in sea-level Oracle Park (13 ft elevation), where cool marine air suppresses carry, yet still set both the single-season (73 in 2001) and all-time career records.

Use the interactive controls below to filter MLB's **Top 30 all-time home run hitters** (every 500-HR club member plus #29t Lou Gehrig and Fred McGriff at 493) by **era**, **batting handedness**, or **individual player**. All selections dynamically update both charts and the sortable leaderboard table.

```{r}
bscols(
  widths = c(5, 3, 4),
  filter_checkbox(
    id = "era_filter",
    label = "Filter by Baseball Era:",
    sharedData = shared_leaders,
    group = ~era
  ),
  filter_checkbox(
    id = "bats_filter",
    label = "Batting Hand:",
    sharedData = shared_leaders,
    group = ~bats_label
  ),
  filter_select(
    id = "player_filter",
    label = "Search / Highlight Hitter(s):",
    sharedData = shared_leaders,
    group = ~player
  )
)
```

### Career Home Run Totals (Top 30 All-Time)

```{r}
plot_ly(
  data = shared_leaders,
  x = ~career_hr,
  y = ~player,
  color = ~era,
  colors = era_colors,
  type = "bar",
  orientation = "h",
  text = ~paste0(
    "<b>#", rank, " ", player, "</b> (", years_active, ")<br>",
    "Primary Franchise: ", franchise, "<br>",
    "Bats: ", bats_label, "<br>",
    "Career Home Runs: <b>", career_hr, "</b><br>",
    "Best Season: ", peak_label, " HR<br>",
    "Pace per 162 Games: ", hr_per_162, " HR<br>",
    "At-Bats per HR: ", ab_per_hr, "<br>",
    "Career Games: ", scales::comma(games)
  ),
  hoverinfo = "text"
) |>
  layout(
    title = "Top 30 All-Time MLB Career Home Run Hitters",
    xaxis = list(title = "Career Home Runs", range = c(0, 810)),
    yaxis = list(title = ""),
    legend = list(orientation = "h", x = 0, y = -0.12),
    height = 700,
    margin = list(l = 145, r = 25, t = 50, b = 75)
  ) |>
  config(displayModeBar = FALSE)
```

### Peak Power Pace vs. Career Longevity

While total home runs reward longevity, comparing **games played** against **home runs per 162 games** reveals two distinct paths to baseball immortality. Pure power-rate outliers like **Mark McGwire** (50.4 HR per 162 games; 10.6 AB/HR) and **Babe Ruth** (46.2 HR per 162 games; 11.8 AB/HR) homered at historic frequencies, whereas ironmen like **Hank Aaron** (3,298 games), **Albert Pujols** (3,080 games), and **Eddie Murray** (3,026 games) sustained elite production over more than 20 seasons. Bubble size reflects each hitter's **single-season home run peak**.

```{r}
plot_ly(
  data = shared_leaders,
  x = ~games,
  y = ~hr_per_162,
  color = ~era,
  colors = era_colors,
  size = ~peak_season_hr,
  sizes = c(12, 34),
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "markers",
  marker = list(opacity = 0.85, line = list(color = "#ffffff", width = 1.5)),
  text = ~paste0(
    "<b>#", rank, " ", player, "</b><br>",
    "Career HRs: <b>", career_hr, "</b> in ", scales::comma(games), " games<br>",
    "Pace: <b>", hr_per_162, " HR / 162 G</b> (", ab_per_hr, " AB/HR)<br>",
    "Single-Season Peak: ", peak_label, " HR<br>",
    "Career RBI: ", scales::comma(career_rbi)
  ),
  hoverinfo = "text"
) |>
  layout(
    title = "Home Run Pace (HR per 162 Games) vs. Career Games Played",
    xaxis = list(title = "Career Games Played", separatethousands = TRUE),
    yaxis = list(title = "Home Runs per 162 Games"),
    legend = list(orientation = "h", x = 0, y = -0.18),
    height = 460,
    margin = list(l = 65, r = 25, t = 50, b = 80)
  ) |>
  config(displayModeBar = FALSE)
```

### Sortable All-Time Home Run Leaderboard

```{r}
datatable(
  shared_leaders,
  rownames = FALSE,
  colnames = c(
    "Rank",
    "Player",
    "Primary Franchise",
    "Era",
    "Bats",
    "Active Years",
    "Career HR",
    "Peak HR (Num)",
    "Best Season",
    "HR / 162 G",
    "AB / HR",
    "Career RBI",
    "Games"
  ),
  options = list(
    pageLength = 15,
    lengthChange = TRUE,
    order = list(list(6, "desc")),
    columnDefs = list(list(visible = FALSE, targets = c(7)))
  )
)
```
